faq: Will a better listing rank higher?
We cannot promise rankings. Shopify's search weighs many signals we do not control. A clear name, honest description and good screenshots help merchants decide, which is what we work on.
Can you add reviews to my listing?
No. We do not write, buy or swap reviews, and doing so breaks Shopify's rules. Reviews have to come from real merchants who used your app.
What do you need from me?
A short description of what the app does, who it is for, your plans and a few screens or a test link. We write everything else and send it for your approval.
Do you follow Shopify's rules on names and icons?
Yes. We check name length, wording, icon size and screenshot rules, and avoid terms Shopify restricts. That reduces the chance of review feedback that delays your launch.
desc:
Shopify App Store listing optimization makes your app clear to merchants who find it while searching. Ecom Swift LLC writes the name, tagline, introduction, feature list and search terms, and designs screenshots with captions, all within Shopify's listing rules.

## What is a Shopify App Store listing?

A Shopify App Store listing is the public page that presents your app to merchants. It holds the app name and tagline, an introduction, a feature list, screenshots or a video, pricing details, support information and search terms. Merchants read it to decide whether to install, so it works as your sales page, your documentation preview and your first impression in one.

## Why does a listing matter for installs?

A merchant arriving at your listing has a problem and very little patience. If the tagline is vague, the screenshots show a login screen and the feature list reads like a database schema, they go back to search results and try another app. Installs are won by clarity: who the app is for, what it does and what it looks like when it works.

The listing also affects discovery. Search inside the App Store uses the words on your listing, so the terms merchants actually type should appear naturally where they belong.

## How wording and visuals change decisions

Merchants think in outcomes: "stop overselling", "send back-in-stock emails", "print packing slips". Technical words describe how the app works, not why they should care. A strong listing opens with the merchant's problem, names the result and then shows proof in screenshots.

Screenshots do much of the talking. A screenshot with a short caption that says what the screen achieves is worth more than a long paragraph. Pricing wording matters as well: clear plan names and limits reduce questions and hesitation.

## What a good App Store listing includes

- An app name and tagline that say what the app does in plain words.
- An introduction that starts with the merchant's problem.
- Feature titles and descriptions written in merchant language.
- Search terms chosen from how real merchants describe the need.
- Screenshots with short captions that show the app in use.
- A pricing section that explains each plan and what it includes.
- Support and FAQ text that answers the first questions.
- An app icon and feature media that meet Shopify's requirements.
- A demo video script and storyboard, in the largest package.

## How we work

We study your app and your merchants, then review a handful of similar listings to see how the category presents itself. We write name and tagline options, the introduction, features and search terms. We check every line against Shopify's listing requirements, so there are no misleading claims, no invented reviews and no ranking promises.

The Basic package delivers clean, ready-to-paste text. Standard adds a first set of screenshots with captions, pricing wording and support text. Premium adds more screenshots, an icon and media check, a video script and the listing entered into your Partner Dashboard for you. Better listings can help merchants understand and choose your app, but search placement depends on factors we cannot control.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Lead with the merchant's problem, not your technology.
- Show real screens from the working app.
- Keep each feature title short and concrete.
- Update the listing when the app changes.

**Avoid:**
- Claims you cannot support, such as comparisons with other apps.
- Stuffing the name or tagline with search terms.
- Screenshots full of tiny text.
- Asking customers for reviews in ways Shopify does not allow.

## Who this service is for

Developers whose app works well but whose listing was written in a hurry. Founders preparing a first submission. Owners of older apps whose listing no longer matches what the app does today.

## What we need from you

A short description of the app and its audience, access to a working version or demo store, your current listing if there is one, and collaborator access to your Partner Dashboard if you want us to enter the listing. We never ask for passwords. Send logos or brand notes if you have them.
